boundary.resolution: Three installed controller word ports retain source requests, mask delivery and clear selected pending bits; source-unit latches and the CPU IE gate remain separate. Cartridge-source names do not add socket programming.

registers.resolution: Complete address/access/reset/32-bit operation reference for FLAGS, ACK and MASK, all eleven named sources and retained unnamed upper bits. Independent live-source review and TS/C++ mapped replay pass.

datapath.resolution: Full-word raise OR, ACK AND NOT, complete MASK replacement and nonzero pending AND mask output are taught with an independently checked numeric trace. Pending is not a FIFO or event count.

visibility.resolution: ACK and MASK apply on accepted writes. Post-entry fresh full FLAGS read is not an acceptance-time snapshot or enabled subset. Independent source review and exact actual-code listings close the observation boundary.

timing.resolution: 33.8688MHz system-cycle unit, ISA base costs, continuing device time during HALT and the actual-example9/6-cycle entry-only budget are explicit. Callback/RET and request waiting are excluded; undefined electrical/controller-rate guarantees remain separate specification decisions in irq-source.md.

interrupts.resolution: CPU IEc and controller gate, shared vector, full flags, STATUS/CAUSE/EPC entry/RFE, no implicit ACK, HALT accepted-event bit and predicate waits are covered. GPU-local/controller rearming, coalescence races and software dispatcher policy are distinct and independently reviewed.

faults.resolution: FLAGS word write READ_ONLY3, low-byte read and invalid subword/offset rules, F32/F64 successive effects, and the already-published common CPU alignment/system fault-latch contract are explicit. Actual mapped TS/C++ fault cases pass.

reset.resolution: Reset pending/MASK/ACK zero words are distinguished from selective ACK or MASK0 and from source-unit reset. Internal save-state/bank fields remain editorial facts, not invented guest words.

programming.resolution: Compact enable, service, acknowledgement and wait sequences connect controller latches, device requests and CPU interrupt acceptance.
